observations.seen: No top spotlight or rim light separates the fighters. In frame 3, Mara Volt's dark brown outfit merges into the dark background. Frames 2 and 4 are lit by flat overcast fill, with no key direction and grey midtones.
The fighters cast almost no shadows. The pale footprint discs under their feet stand in for contact shadows. The statues, braziers and throne show no grounded shadows on the floor in any frame.

The Crown Arena floor in frames 1 and 3 has glossy reflections of the gold lines and props, and the gold trim reads as metallic. The daytime venues in frames 2 and 4 show matte floors with no environment reflection.

The venues are prop-rich: a throne with crown, dragon statues, braziers, a castle, and a shrine with prayer flags. The styles clash, with a hand-painted cartoon castle next to semi-realistic statues. The crowd is flat black blob silhouettes with white square lights. The sky in frames 2 and 4 is a blank grey gradient.
There is no haze or volumetric spotlight cone. The only atmosphere is a few ember specks at the top of frames 1 and 3 and floating white orbs in frame 4. Depth falloff is not visible.

The throne leather, gold crown and emissive green dragon trims hold up. The fighters' cloth and skin look plasticky with uniform roughness. The floors are flat colour, and the castle textures are stylised in a different language from everything else.

The fighter faces are crude, and Mara Volt's silhouette is low detail. The trees and palms are low-poly cards. In frame 4 the shrine shows a ghosted, overlapping pink translucent duplicate that looks like a sorting or transition artefact.

In frames 2 to 4 the fighters sit at the far left and right edges, leaving a large empty centre dominated by the floor emblem. The pair does not form a readable focal unit. In frame 1, Kenji fills the left foreground while Mara is cut off at the top edge.

The side-on framing is consistent in frames 2 to 4 but pulled wide. In frame 1, Mara is airborne and cropped by the top of the frame behind the HUD. Kenji is very close, so the camera does not keep both fighters in frame.

Frames 2 and 4 have a heavy vignette and a grey low-contrast wash. Bloom on the gold is mild and inconsistent. There is no arena-fight grade, such as crushed blacks with warm highlights, on the daytime venues.
The fighters hold near-identical stiff guard poses across frames, with flat hands and little weight shift. Mara's jump pose in frame 1 is mostly off-screen and does not read.

The HUD in frame 1 is clean, with named health bars, a super meter, a round clock and a control strip. The browser-style top navigation tabs (Quick Bout, Combo Lab, and so on) sit over the game and break immersion. The HUD appears in only one frame.

nextChange.change: add the recipe row's atmosphere (fog scale, haze, shafts) at the look's intensity
